subproblem.title: Weighted approximate tangent planes are local
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, O ⊆ ℝ^N open, M ⊆ ℝ^N, θ : ℝ^N → ℝ, y ∈ O and P ≤ ℝ^N a linear subspace. Then O ∩ M has weighted approximate tangent space P at y with respect to θ (Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (O ∩ M) θ y P) if and only if M has weighted approximate tangent space P at y with respect to θ (Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y P).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (O M : Set (Euclidean N)) (θ : Euclidean N → ℝ) (y : Euclidean N) (P : Submodule ℝ (Euclidean N)), IsOpen O → y ∈ O → (Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (O ∩ M) θ y P ↔ Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y P)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation.
- H^n := μHE[n] on ℝ^N = Euclidean N, and blowUpMap x r z := r^{-1}·(z − x).
- For an arbitrary set A, the set integral ∫_A g dH^n means ∫ g d(H^n⌞A).
- By definition, Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S θ x P holds iff finrank P = n and, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ), ∫_{blowUpMap x r '' S} f(v)·θ(x + r·v) dH^n(v) → θ(x)·∫_P f dH^n as r → 0 along 𝓝[>] 0.

1. Reduction. Both predicates contain the same conjunct finrank P = n, and for each f the same prescribed limit θ(y)·∫_P f dH^n. For f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ) put
   F_1(r) := ∫_{blowUpMap y r '' (O ∩ M)} f(v)·θ(y + r·v) dH^n(v),
   F_2(r) := ∫_{blowUpMap y r '' M} f(v)·θ(y + r·v) dH^n(v).
It suffices to show, for every f, that F_1(r) = F_2(r) for all r in some interval (0, δ) with δ > 0. Then F_1 =ᶠ[𝓝[>]0] F_2 because (0, δ) ∈ 𝓝[>]0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT). Filter.tendsto_congr' then turns each limit statement into the other, which gives both directions of the equivalence.

2. Choice of radii. Fix f.
   - tsupport f is compact, hence bounded. So tsupport f ⊆ closedBall(0, R₀) for some R₀ (HasCompactSupport.isBounded, Bornology.IsBounded.subset_closedBall).
   - Put R := max(R₀, 1) > 0 and B := closedBall(0, R). Then tsupport f ⊆ B.
   - Since O is open and y ∈ O, there is ε > 0 with ball(y, ε) ⊆ O (Metric.isOpen_iff).
   - Let δ := ε/R > 0 and fix r with 0 < r < δ.

3. Cut-off identity. Put h(v) := f(v)·θ(y + r·v). If v ∉ B, then v ∉ tsupport f, so f(v) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and h(v) = 0. Hence, for every set A ⊆ ℝ^N,
   ∫_A h dH^n = ∫ h d(H^n⌞A) = ∫_B h d(H^n⌞A) = ∫ h d(H^n⌞(B ∩ A)).
   - The first equality is the notation.
   - The second is setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero, applied to the measure H^n⌞A and the set B. It has no integrability or measurability hypothesis.
   - The third rewrites the measure (H^n⌞A)⌞B = H^n⌞(B ∩ A) by Measure.restrict_restrict (B is closed, hence measurable).
   So no integrability of h is needed.

4. Set identity: B ∩ blowUpMap y r '' (O ∩ M) = B ∩ blowUpMap y r '' M.
   - ⊆ holds because O ∩ M ⊆ M.
   - For ⊇, let v ∈ B with v = r^{-1}·(z − y) for some z ∈ M. Then r^{-1}·‖z − y‖ = ‖v‖ ≤ R (norm_smul, r > 0). So ‖z − y‖ ≤ r·R < (ε/R)·R = ε.
   - Thus z ∈ ball(y, ε) ⊆ O, so z ∈ O ∩ M and v = blowUpMap y r z ∈ blowUpMap y r '' (O ∩ M).

5. Apply step 3 to the two image sets and use step 4: for every r ∈ (0, δ),
   F_1(r) = ∫ h d(H^n⌞(B ∩ blowUpMap y r '' (O ∩ M))) = ∫ h d(H^n⌞(B ∩ blowUpMap y r '' M)) = F_2(r).

6. By step 1, Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (O ∩ M) θ y P ↔ Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ y P. ∎
proof_key_steps: Both predicates have the same finrank condition and the same prescribed limits. So it suffices that the blow-up integrals for O ∩ M and for M agree for all small r > 0.
Choose R > 0 with tsupport f ⊆ closedBall(0,R) and ε > 0 with ball(y,ε) ⊆ O. Take 0 < r < ε/R.
Since f vanishes off closedBall(0,R), ∫_A f(v)θ(y+rv) dH^n = ∫ … d(H^n⌞(closedBall(0,R) ∩ A)) for every set A.
closedBall(0,R) ∩ blowUpMap y r '' (O ∩ M) = closedBall(0,R) ∩ blowUpMap y r '' M, because ‖z − y‖ ≤ rR < ε forces z ∈ O.
Eventually equal functions have the same limits along 𝓝[>]0 (tendsto_congr').

audit.reason: All hypotheses appear in both formulations. The compact-support radius and open neighborhood give eventual equality of the blow-up integrals. The cited cut-off lemma requires no integrability, and restrict_restrict only requires the closed ball to be measurable, so arbitrary M and θ cause no gap. Eventual equality proves both directions with the common dimension condition.

subproblem.title: Weighted approximate tangent planes are invariant under the similarity y ↦ ξ + t·y
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^N, θ : ℝ^N → ℝ, ξ, y ∈ ℝ^N, t > 0, P ≤ ℝ^N a linear subspace, and σ(w) := ξ + t·w. Then σ^{-1}(M) has weighted approximate tangent space P at y with respect to θ∘σ if and only if M has weighted approximate tangent space P at σ(y) = ξ + t·y with respect to θ (both in the sense of Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclidean N)) (θ : Euclidean N → ℝ) (ξ y : Euclidean N) (t : ℝ) (P : Submodule ℝ (Euclidean N)), 0 < t → (Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n ((fun w : Euclidean N ↦ ξ + t • w) ⁻¹' M) (fun w : Euclidean N ↦ θ (ξ + t • w)) y P ↔ Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ (ξ + t • y) P)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation.
- H^n := μHE[n] on ℝ^N = Euclidean N, and blowUpMap x r z := r^{-1}·(z − x).
- For an arbitrary set A, ∫_A g dH^n means ∫ g d(H^n⌞A).
- By definition, Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n S θ' x P holds iff finrank P = n and, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ), ∫_{blowUpMap x r '' S} f(v)·θ'(x + r·v) dH^n(v) → θ'(x)·∫_P f dH^n along 𝓝[>] 0.
- Put σ(w) := ξ + t·w, x := σ(y) = ξ + t·y, and m(r) := t·r.

1. Reduction. Both predicates contain the conjunct finrank P = n. For f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ) put
   F_1(r) := ∫_{blowUpMap y r '' σ^{-1}(M)} f(v)·θ(σ(y + r·v)) dH^n(v),
   F_2(s) := ∫_{blowUpMap x s '' M} f(v)·θ(x + s·v) dH^n(v).
The prescribed limits (θ∘σ)(y)·∫_P f dH^n and θ(x)·∫_P f dH^n are the same number L_f. So it suffices to show, for every f, that F_1 → L_f along 𝓝[>]0 if and only if F_2 → L_f along 𝓝[>]0.

2. Equality of blow-up sets: for every r ∈ ℝ, blowUpMap y r '' σ^{-1}(M) = blowUpMap x (t·r) '' M.
   - (⊆) Let v = r^{-1}·(w − y) with σ(w) ∈ M, and put z := σ(w) ∈ M. Then z − x = (ξ + t·w) − (ξ + t·y) = t·(w − y). So blowUpMap x (t·r) z = ((t·r)^{-1}·t)·(w − y) = (t^{-1}·r^{-1}·t)·(w − y) = r^{-1}·(w − y) = v. Here (t·r)^{-1} = t^{-1}·r^{-1} holds in ℝ even for r = 0, since 0^{-1} = 0, and t^{-1}·t = 1.
   - (⊇) Let v = (t·r)^{-1}·(z − x) with z ∈ M, and put w := t^{-1}·(z − ξ). Then σ(w) = ξ + t·t^{-1}·(z − ξ) = z ∈ M, so w ∈ σ^{-1}(M). Moreover blowUpMap y r w = r^{-1}·(t^{-1}·(z − ξ) − y) = (r^{-1}·t^{-1})·(z − ξ − t·y) = (t·r)^{-1}·(z − (ξ + t·y)) = v.

3. Equality of integrands: for all r and v, σ(y + r·v) = ξ + t·y + (t·r)·v = x + (t·r)·v (smul_add, smul_smul, add_assoc). With step 2 this gives F_1(r) = F_2(t·r) for every r ∈ ℝ, i.e. F_1 = F_2 ∘ m.

4. Reparametrization of the filter.
   - Since t > 0, comap m (𝓝[>]0) = 𝓝[>]0 (comap_mulLeft_nhdsGT_zero).
   - m is surjective (m(t^{-1}·s) = s). So map m (𝓝[>]0) = map m (comap m (𝓝[>]0)) = 𝓝[>]0 (Filter.map_comap_of_surjective).
   - Hence, for every filter L on ℝ: Tendsto (F_2 ∘ m) (𝓝[>]0) L ↔ Tendsto F_2 (map m (𝓝[>]0)) L ↔ Tendsto F_2 (𝓝[>]0) L (Filter.tendsto_map'_iff).

5. By steps 3 and 4 with L := 𝓝 L_f, for every f: Tendsto F_1 (𝓝[>]0) (𝓝 L_f) ↔ Tendsto F_2 (𝓝[>]0) (𝓝 L_f). Together with the common conjunct finrank P = n (step 1), this proves Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (σ^{-1}(M)) (θ∘σ) y P ↔ Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ (ξ + t·y) P. ∎
proof_key_steps: Both predicates have the same finrank condition. The prescribed limits coincide because (θ∘σ)(y) = θ(σ(y)).
For every r, blowUpMap y r '' σ^{-1}(M) = blowUpMap σ(y) (t·r) '' M.
σ(y + r·v) = σ(y) + (t·r)·v, hence F_1(r) = F_2(t·r) for all r.
r ↦ t·r maps 𝓝[>]0 onto 𝓝[>]0 (comap_mulLeft_nhdsGT_zero and map_comap_of_surjective). So F_1 and F_2 have the same limits along 𝓝[>]0.

audit.reason: The exact type matches the prose. The inverse-similarity calculations establish equality of blow-up sets, including r = 0, and the integrands and prescribed limits coincide. Positive multiplication maps the right-neighborhood filter onto itself, proving both convergence directions. The supplied argument is complete, self-contained and non-circular.

subproblem.title: Countable n-rectifiability is preserved by the inverse similarity
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, ξ ∈ ℝ^N, t > 0 and M ⊆ ℝ^N. Suppose M is countably n-rectifiable in the sense of Chapter03.CountablyRectifiable: there are a set M₀ ⊆ ℝ^N with H^n(M₀) = 0 (H^n = μHE[n]) and Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝ^n → ℝ^N (j ∈ ℕ) with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n). Then σ^{-1}(M) = {y ∈ ℝ^N : ξ + t·y ∈ M} is countably n-rectifiable, where σ(y) := ξ + t·y.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (ξ : Euclidean N) (t : ℝ) (M : Set (Euclidean N)), 0 < t → Chapter03.CountablyRectifiable n M → Chapter03.CountablyRectifiable n ((fun y : Euclidean N ↦ ξ + t • y) ⁻¹' M)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation. H^n := μHE[n] on ℝ^N = Euclidean N. Put σ(y) := ξ + t·y and η(x) := t^{-1}·(x − ξ). Since t ≠ 0, η(σ(y)) = y and σ(η(x)) = x. Chapter03.CountablyRectifiable n S means: there are M₀ with H^n(M₀) = 0 and maps F_j : ℝ^n → ℝ^N (j ∈ ℕ), each Lipschitz with some constant K_j ∈ ℝ≥0, such that S ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j range F_j.

1. Unpack the hypothesis for M. This gives M₀ with H^n(M₀) = 0 and maps F_j with Lipschitz constants K_j, such that M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j range F_j.

2. η is Lipschitz with constant ‖t^{-1}‖₊.
   - For x, x' ∈ ℝ^N, η(x) − η(x') = t^{-1}·(x − x') (smul_sub, sub_sub_sub_cancel_right).
   - So dist(η x, η x') = |t^{-1}|·dist(x, x') (norm_smul), which gives the Lipschitz bound (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul).
   - Hence G_j := η ∘ F_j : ℝ^n → ℝ^N is Lipschitz with constant ‖t^{-1}‖₊·K_j (LipschitzWith.comp).

3. The new exceptional set is M₀' := σ^{-1}(M₀). We show it is H^n-null.
   - First, σ^{-1}(M₀) = t^{-1}·{−ξ + x : x ∈ M₀}. If ξ + t·y ∈ M₀, then y = t^{-1}·(−ξ + (ξ + t·y)). Conversely, ξ + t·(t^{-1}·(−ξ + x)) = x.
   - The translation x ↦ −ξ + x is an isometry (isometry_add_left (−ξ)), so it preserves H^n of every set (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image).
   - Since t^{-1} ≠ 0, H^n(t^{-1}·X) = ‖t^{-1}‖₊^n • H^n(X) for every X (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀; write the image under x ↦ t^{-1}·x as the pointwise dilate via Set.image_smul).
   - Therefore H^n(M₀') = ‖t^{-1}‖₊^n • H^n(M₀) = ‖t^{-1}‖₊^n • 0 = 0.

4. Covering. Let y ∈ σ^{-1}(M), so σ(y) ∈ M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j range F_j.
   - If σ(y) ∈ M₀, then y ∈ M₀'.
   - Otherwise σ(y) = F_j(v) for some j ∈ ℕ and v ∈ ℝ^n. Then G_j(v) = η(F_j(v)) = η(σ(y)) = t^{-1}·(t·y) = y (add_sub_cancel_left, smul_smul, inv_mul_cancel₀, one_smul). So y ∈ range G_j.

5. Thus σ^{-1}(M) ⊆ M₀' ∪ ⋃_j range G_j, where H^n(M₀') = 0 by step 3 and each G_j is Lipschitz by step 2. This is exactly Chapter03.CountablyRectifiable n (σ^{-1}(M)), with witnesses M₀' and (G_j)_j. ∎
proof_key_steps: Unpack M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ^n) with H^n(M₀) = 0 and each F_j Lipschitz.
η(x) = t^{-1}(x − ξ) is ‖t^{-1}‖₊-Lipschitz, so each G_j := η ∘ F_j is Lipschitz.
σ^{-1}(M₀) = t^{-1}·(−ξ + M₀) is H^n-null by translation invariance and euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀.
Every y ∈ σ^{-1}(M) lies in σ^{-1}(M₀) or equals G_j(v), where σ(y) = F_j(v).

audit.reason: The statement matches CountablyRectifiable exactly. The proof constructs the inverse-image exceptional set, proves its Hausdorff measure is zero directly from library scaling, supplies Lipschitz parametrizations with explicit constants, and verifies their covering property. Positivity ensures the inverse similarity exists. No sibling or parent theorem is assumed.

subproblem.title: Restricted Hausdorff measure under the similarity y ↦ ξ + t·y
subproblem.statement: Let N, n ∈ ℕ, ξ ∈ ℝ^N, t > 0 and σ : ℝ^N → ℝ^N, σ(y) := ξ + t·y. Let H^n = μHE[n] be Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure on ℝ^N = Euclidean N. Then for every set A ⊆ ℝ^N, measurable or not, H^n⌞σ(A) = t^n·σ_#(H^n⌞A) as measures on ℝ^N. That is, (μHE[n]).restrict (σ '' A) = ENNReal.ofReal (t^n) • ((μHE[n]).restrict A).map σ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (N n : ℕ) (ξ : Euclidean N) (t : ℝ) (A : Set (Euclidean N)), 0 < t → (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)).restrict ((fun y : Euclidean N ↦ ξ + t • y) '' A) = ENNReal.ofReal (t ^ n) • ((μHE[n] : Measure (Euclidean N)).restrict A).map (fun y : Euclidean N ↦ ξ + t • y)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation. H^n := μHE[n] on ℝ^N = Euclidean N. It is a Borel measure, and its value on an arbitrary set is the outer-measure value. Put σ(y) := ξ + t·y and c := ENNReal.ofReal(t^n). Fix an arbitrary set A ⊆ ℝ^N.

1. σ is continuous, being a constant plus a scalar multiple of the identity. Hence it is Borel measurable.

2. Scaling of arbitrary sets. We claim H^n(σ(S)) = c·H^n(S) for every S ⊆ ℝ^N.
   - Write σ(S) = τ(t·S), where τ(z) := ξ + z and t·S := {t·s : s ∈ S} is the pointwise dilate (Set.image_smul, Set.image_image).
   - τ is an isometry of ℝ^N (isometry_add_left ξ). So H^n(τ(X)) = H^n(X) for every X ⊆ ℝ^N (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image).
   - Since t ≠ 0, H^n(t·S) = ‖t‖₊^n • H^n(S) for every S (MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀).
   - Since t > 0, the ℝ≥0-scalar ‖t‖₊^n acts on [0,∞] as multiplication by ENNReal.ofReal(t^n) = c (ENNReal.smul_def, ENNReal.ofReal_coe_nnreal, NNReal.coe_pow, coe_nnnorm, Real.norm_of_nonneg).
   - Therefore H^n(σ(S)) = H^n(τ(t·S)) = H^n(t·S) = c·H^n(S).

3. Evaluate both measures on a Borel set B ⊆ ℝ^N.
   - Left side: (H^n⌞σ(A))(B) = H^n(B ∩ σ(A)) by Measure.restrict_apply. This needs only B to be measurable; A is arbitrary.
   - Right side: (c • σ_#(H^n⌞A))(B) = c·(H^n⌞A)(σ^{-1}(B)), by Measure.smul_apply and Measure.map_apply (σ and B are measurable).
   - This equals c·H^n(σ^{-1}(B) ∩ A), by Measure.restrict_apply for the measurable set σ^{-1}(B).

4. Set identity: B ∩ σ(A) = σ(A) ∩ B = σ(A ∩ σ^{-1}(B)) = σ(σ^{-1}(B) ∩ A). The middle equality is Set.image_inter_preimage, which holds for every map.

5. Apply step 4, then step 2 with S := σ^{-1}(B) ∩ A: H^n(B ∩ σ(A)) = H^n(σ(σ^{-1}(B) ∩ A)) = c·H^n(σ^{-1}(B) ∩ A). By step 3, the two measures agree on every Borel set B.

6. Two measures on ℝ^N that agree on all measurable sets are equal (Measure.ext). Hence (μHE[n]).restrict (σ '' A) = ENNReal.ofReal(t^n) • ((μHE[n]).restrict A).map σ. ∎
proof_key_steps: σ = (ξ + ·) ∘ (t • ·). Translation invariance (an isometry) and euclideanHausdorffMeasure_smul₀ give H^n(σ(S)) = t^n·H^n(S) for every set S.
For Borel B, (H^n⌞σ(A))(B) = H^n(B ∩ σ(A)) and (t^n·σ_#(H^n⌞A))(B) = t^n·H^n(σ^{-1}(B) ∩ A).
Since B ∩ σ(A) = σ(σ^{-1}(B) ∩ A), the scaling identity makes the two values equal. Conclude by Measure.ext.

audit.reason: The prose and Lean type agree, including arbitrary, possibly nonmeasurable A. Translation invariance and positive dilation give the required scaling on every set. Evaluation on measurable B uses restrict_apply and map_apply with exactly their required hypotheses; the image-intersection identity then proves measure equality. The proof is complete and independent.
